introduction: This developer uses AI to turn an uncertain idea into a clear, testable result. They welcome suggestions about the route, while keeping responsibility for the destination. Their most distinctive habit is to separate discussing a change from authorizing it.

chapters.title: The work starts before the code
chapters.body: A fictional interface task begins with a pause: the developer asks for steps and risks before implementation. The request gives the agent a concrete role in clarifying the work. It also creates a point where the developer can choose a direction before changes accumulate.

evidence.quote: Before editing, outline the steps and the risks. Wait for my choice.

chapters.title: Freedom within a clear boundary
chapters.body: Once the direction is agreed, they give the agent room to choose the implementation. The boundary concerns the observable result: an existing API must keep working. In this conversation, delegation and control coexist because they apply to different decisions.

evidence.quote: Choose the implementation, but preserve the existing API.

chapters.title: Verification is part of the handoff
chapters.body: A separate task shows the same attention to completion conditions. The developer asks for checks and a description of their limits. This demonstrates a request for evidence, rather than proving that the implementation succeeded. Together, the conversations suggest a collaborator who delegates execution while keeping the final judgment close.

evidence.quote: Run the relevant checks and explain what they do not cover.
